name: Dossier - Generated Case File Spread for Mystery Games
summary: Composes an open manila case file from your mystery game's own suspects, clues and statements: typed forms, booking photographs, stamps, redactions and red-pencil marks.
description:
Your mystery game already knows its suspects, clues and statements. Dossier types them up.

Hand Dossier a case (people, evidence, statements) and it composes an open manila case file on a lamp-lit desk: a suspect roster typed onto a printed form with a booking photograph beside every name, an evidence index with redaction bars wherever your data says a fact is unknown, carbon copies and telex strips for the statements, rubber stamps struck in red, a paperclip, a strip of evidence tape, and the investigator's red-pencil marks in the margins. The result is an ordinary Texture2D for uGUI, UI Toolkit or a material in your scene.

None of it is an imported image. Every sheet, stamp, clip and line of type is drawn in code by a software rasteriser shipped in the package, and the lettering is filled from the outlines of three real typefaces (Oswald, Courier Prime and Caveat), included under the SIL Open Font License.

THE LAYOUT ANSWERS THE DATA

Three people get full-width cards with large photographs; ten get a two-column roster. Seven clues get two lines each with their descriptions; twenty get a two-column index. A cold case is typed on yellowed, foxed paper; a classified one on onionskin, redacted hard. A suspect's status strikes its stamp across their photograph (SUSPECT, CLEARED, CHARGED, DECEASED, MISSING, WITNESS, INFORMANT, PERSON OF INTEREST, UNIDENTIFIED). A key clue linked to a suspect gets a red-pencil arrow across the spread to that person's photograph, and the most-linked suspect has their name circled. An interview is a carbon copy; a phone call, telegram or radio message is a telex strip; low reliability earns a "doubtful" query in the margin.

UNKNOWN IS A WORD, NOT A BLANK

An empty field is simply not typed. A field that says it is unknown (?, unknown, redacted, classified, withheld) is blacked out, weighted by what the fact is: a withheld name is blocked out, an alias gets a marker bar, an age is struck through. A sentence that merely contains the word is data and is typed.

52 HAND-AUTHORED MOTIFS IN 10 FAMILIES

Stamps (8), fasteners (6), tapes (4), folder tabs (6), photo mountings (4), typed blocks (5), hand marks (8), paper stocks (4: bond, aged, onionskin, ledger), stains (4) and redactions (3). The editor window's motif sheet draws every one of them from the shipped code.

NOTHING IS STRUCK OVER A NAME

Every stamp, clip, strip of tape and coffee ring is placed by searching candidate spots for one that misses the record. A name, a title, a face, the booking placard and a solid redaction bar are refused outright. The red-pencil arrow goes through the same search, and when a crowded card leaves no clear approach it stops at the circled name instead of ruling through the file.

GETTING STARTED

1. Import the package. Everything lands under Assets/CSAF/Dossier/.
2. Open Demo/Scenes/DossierDemo.unity and press Play. Four sample cases (active, cold, closed and classified) are composed; LEFT and RIGHT page between them.
3. Open Tools > CSAF > Dossier, pick a case and press Compose spread. Beside the spread, the window explains every choice and the word in your data that caused it.
4. To author a case without code: Assets > Create > CSAF > Dossier Case File, fill in the Inspector, and press Compose this case in Dossier.
5. From code: build a CaseFile, load the shipped typefaces with DossierType.FromAssets, and call DossierSpread.Compose. For anything a player opens, compose off the main thread.
technical:
Features: case file spread generated from your own suspect, clue and statement data; 52 hand-authored motifs in 10 families, including 4 paper stocks; included CPU rasteriser, TrueType outline reader and typesetter; layout that adapts to the number of suspects, clues and statements; placement search that never strikes a mark across a name, face, placard or redaction bar; ScriptableObject case assets; editor window with a derivation panel and motif sheet; thread-safe bake path; deterministic output.

Number of C# scripts: 34 (30 Runtime, 3 Editor, 1 Demo). Visual Scripting graphs: 0.
Assemblies: CSAF.Dossier.Runtime (all platforms), CSAF.Dossier.Editor (Editor only), CSAF.Dossier.Demo (demo scene component).
Editor window: Tools > CSAF > Dossier. Demo scene: Assets/CSAF/Dossier/Demo/Scenes/DossierDemo.unity (OnGUI, no Canvas).
Minimum Unity version: 2022.3. Built and tested against 6000.5.7f1.
Render pipelines: Built-In, URP and HDRP. The spread is rasterised into a Texture2D on the CPU and never touches the render pipeline.
No Resources folder, no shaders, no images, no network calls. Dependencies: none.
Limits: TrueType fonts only, no complex-script shaping; up to 10 suspect cards, 24 clues and 4 statements per spread.
Asset uses Oswald, Courier Prime and Caveat under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; see Third-Party Notices.txt in the package for details.

Documentation: https://github.com/onefreeman1337/csaf-releases/blob/main/docs/dossier/README.md
ai:
All of the C# in this package was written by an AI coding agent (Anthropic Claude) under human direction. That covers the software rasteriser, the TrueType outline reader and typesetter, the motif corpus, the case model and its derivation rules, the spread composer, the editor window and the demo scene.

The spreads the package produces are not made by an image model. Every sheet, stamp, clip, photograph and line of type is drawn by the shipped code from authored geometry, offline. The three typefaces are third-party fonts by their own authors, shipped unmodified under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. The store images are captures and composites of the package's output. Some of them, including the cover, set that output over an AI-generated illustrated background.

No audio is included, because the package contains no audio of any kind. Text and dialog: no.
